f201.text: Last time, we counted legs. Insects have six. And we met the reptiles, with dry, scaly skin. Like Basil!

f3g3.text: Same and different, with a reason.

f301.text: Lock in first. A little squirrel is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

f401.text: Round one. This animal has wings. It flies. Is a bat a bird? One, yes. Two, no. Show me with your fingers.

f403.text: One! It flies, like a bird!

f404.text: Two! I think I see fur.

f501.text: Be a hair! Shrink down. Quietly.

f502.text: You are one hair on a fruit bat's back. Soft fur, like a forest, all around you.

f503.text: It spreads its wings. Thin skin. No feathers!

f504.text: Whoosh! Out into the night. The air is cool. But the body under you stays warm.

f505.text: Back at the palm, a baby bat drinks its mother's milk.

f601.text: The answer is two. A bat is not a bird. It is a mammal!

f605.text: Mammals are animals that have hair or fur as their outer covering.

f701.text: Monkeys, cats, bats, and you! They all have hair or fur.

f702b.text: And I'm the reptile. No fur for me!

f703.text: Most mammals give birth to their young alive. The females have mammary glands that can produce milk for their young.

f704.text: Mammals are warm-blooded, which means that they can maintain a constant body temperature.

f801.text: Exam tip! Compare a bat and a bird.

f802.text: A bat and a bird are similar because both have wings. They are different because a bat has fur, but a bird has feathers.

f901.text: Round two. Which one does not belong? One, a cat. Two, a monkey. Three, a lizard. Show me with your fingers.

f903.text: Two. The monkey. It climbs trees.

f906.text: The answer is three. Find what the others share. A cat and a monkey have fur: mammals. A lizard has dry, scaly skin: a reptile.

f908b.text: Scales, not fur. The odd one out is me!

f1001.text: One. It has scaly skin. Two. It breathes air with its lungs. Three. It swims in the sea, so it is a fish!

f1002.text: Showdown! Double points. One line has a mistake. Line one, two, or three? Show me with your fingers.

f1004.text: Three. Fish usually breathe through gills.

f1007.text: Read all the clues. Scaly skin and lungs: a reptile. It is a sea turtle!

f1008.text: Showed three fingers? Put up two more on your score hand!

c1103.text: Six legs? Insect! Dry, scaly skin? Reptile! Hair or fur? Mammal!

f1203.text: Living things such as plants and animals can be classified based on common observable characteristics. There are different types of plants and animals.

f1301.text: Show me your score hand! More than two? You beat the Buddies. Four fingers? High five!

f1302.text: Did you spot the squirrel? It was on the palm trunk! Is it cold-blooded, or warm-blooded? Tell someone at home.

f1401.text: Next time: fungi and bacteria! Mould on bread. Yeast, for making bread. Both are fungi! Which one is useful? Lock in your answer!
